Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (BrightBank)

Sofia —

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xx responses from requests routed to our reserved capacity (pool id: BB-RSV-12). Impact started ~08:45 PT and has been persistent for ~20 minutes. Key signals from our side:
- 99th pctl generation latency jumped from ~220ms to 1.8s
- ~2% 502/503 rate across production traffic during the window
- Request queue depth on our side spiked; downstream clients are timing out

This is affecting credit-authorize flows for a subset of merchants; we need this triaged urgently and would like a short bridge call if possible. Please advise immediate next steps and whether you see any mitigation we should apply client-side.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: ACTION: BrightBank reserved pool saturation — urgent mitigation requests

Sofia / team — quick summary from runtime:
- Observation: A concentrated burst of long-context requests (seq len > 1024) from a BrightBank canary traffic shard caused persistent KV-cache churn on BB-RSV-12 hosts. Continuous batching combined with the request shape exhausted the host headroom and bumped into kernel-level queuing; autoscale policy did not trigger because the per-node scheduler reported CPU nominal while queuing occurred in the token emission path.
- Symptoms: High 99p latency and elevated 502/503s from the model runtime's retry gate.

Immediate mitigations applied (now):
1) Triggered pool expansion: +25% ephemeral capacity from dedicated spare nodes (BB-temp-01..03). Expected to reduce queueing in ~90s.
2) Enabled route-level fallback for low-priority routes -> hosted-quantized variant (same model family) for non-critical merchant flows (applied at 09:33 PT).
3) Disabled continuous-batching for the long-context shard to avoid KV thrash; this will increase per-token CPU but reduce queuing.
4) Warm-started KV cache from snapshot for the affected model variant.

Follow-ups (next 24h):
- Work with infra on a fix to autoscale visibility for token queue length (ticket INF-7421).
- Produce a short RCA and change request to make the reserved routing respect sequence-length-based capacity steering.

Attached: pool snapshot + quick runbook for the temporary steps.

[Attachment: pool_metrics_20270523.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]
[Attachment: mitigation_runbook_v2.md (MD, 18KB)]

I'll join the customer bridge in 10.

— Aditya
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Sofia / Execs / Customer —

Quick customer-facing summary and asks:
- What happened: A sudden long-context traffic burst from BrightBank's canary caused sustained KV-cache churn on their reserved pool (BB-RSV-12), producing high tail latency and ~2% 5xxs for ~40 minutes.
- What we did: engineering expanded ephemeral capacity, enabled hosted fallback for non-critical traffic, disabled continuous batching for the shard, and warm-started caches. Immediate consumer impact reduced; current 99p latency back to ~240ms.
- Customer ask: BrightBank has asked for an explanation, assurance on prevention, and consideration for transaction credits for failed requests during the window.

Requesting executive attention for two items:
1) Pre-approve a one-off customer credit (sales ops/legal) up to $15k while we complete a quantified loss calc. This allows Marissa to close comms without delays.
2) Sign-off for a short-term prioritized infra change (INF-7421) to alter autoscale to surface token-queue metrics into scaling decisions — estimated 2 engineer-weeks; request is to green-light immediate prioritization.

I'll share the RCA draft after infra and runtime confirm root cause components. Meeting: I've proposed a 30-minute bridge with BrightBank at Tue May 25 10:00 PT; Ellen confirmed availability below. Please advise if execs want to join.

— Marissa Cole
